newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil hit by falling futures, but prems hold.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil hit by falling futures, but prems hold.

text.p: NWE gas oil took a tumble even though premiums held broadly steady because IPE futures dropped nearly $4 a tonne.
March IPE gas oil ended down $3.75 at $167.00 a tonne as the market followed the U.S. lower.

Premiums were holding up fairly well with the exception of narrowly easier diesel. Barges talked around March IPE +$1.50 on the bid to +$2.50 on the offer for much of the day for Rotterdam material and one Antwerp barge sold in the morning at +$1.50.

Russian material also saw more activity. A 25,000 tonne cargo sold at March IPE +$1.75 cif ARA in the north while two Russian cargoes were done in the Mediterranean, both around high cif quotes flat to +$1.
FOD material was quieter, but premiums were thought to be roughly steady or very narrowly weaker around March IPE +$4-5 cif NWE with DIN spec product about $1 higher.

Diesel premiums hovered around March IPE +$15-16 cif NWE with one deal confirmed at +$16 and rumours of a second also done at +$16. Buying interest into France was heard around +$15.50, but demand was likely to ease once the Donges refinery comes back on stream later this week.
